newsitem.title: USA: Palomar Medical receives EpiLaser patent.
newsitem.headline: Palomar Medical receives EpiLaser patent.

text.p: Palomar Medical Technologies Inc said it has been issued a U.S. patent protecting its laser-based hair removal technology, called EpiLaser.

The company said it holds the exclusive worldwide license for the technology, which was developed at Massachusetts General Hospital. EpiLaser received U.S. Food and Drug Administration marketing clearance Monday.

Palomar said the patented technology, which is being disputed by MEHL/Biophile International Corp in a lawsuit filed in New Jersey district court, is based on 10 years of research at Massachusetts General and covers a method for hair removal from any part of the body coupled with a technique for avoiding epidermal damage through precision cooling.

MEHL/Biophile contends that Palomar infringed on a patented method of laser hair removal that MEHL holds an exclusive license for and alleged that Palomar marketed its product before receiving FDA clearance. Palomar denied these allegations.
"We've had attorneys look at the lawsuit and there seems to be absolutely no basis for it," said John Ingoldsby, Palomar's director of investor relations.

"The main difference is that the epidermis is protected by a cooling process (with EpiLaser). There is absolutely no cooling implied or stated in MEHL's patent. We use cooling and that is the subject of the patent we announced today," Ingoldsby said.
"We have thoroughly and laboriously researched the possibility of infringing on (MEHL's) patent and we are absolutely confident that we are not doing so."

Palomar said that a number of laser hair removal technique patents have been issued over the past several years, but stated it believes some licensees are not using technology as disclosed in their patents. It said that in some cases it believes these licensees have adopted techniques similar to those described in the Massachusetts General patent.
"If and when other laser hair removal devices using such techniques appear in the U.S. market, we are fully prepared to enforce our proprietary positions," Palomar president Michael Smotrich said.

As part of the multi-year agreement with Massachusetts General Hospital, Palomar said its scientists and engineers are working closely with the hospital to optimize and improve its hair removal technology. These efforts have resulted in a number of additional patent applications by Massachusetts General and Palomar, which will be issued in the near future, according to the company.
